title: Dialogue-chunk adaptive batcher and KV reservation study for mixed-length workloads
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Customer workloads show high variance in prompt/response length within single sessions (few-shot prompts followed by long reasoning responses and short followups). Our continuous batcher currently coalesces by arrival time and coarse length buckets; this leads to suboptimal KV residency, increased GPU memory fragmentation, and p99 latency spikes when long-response requests displace cached prefixes.

Goal:
Design and validate an adaptive 'dialogue-chunk' coalescing scheduler that: (1) splits incoming interactions into stable prefix chunks + generative chunks, (2) maintains a small per-chunk KV reservation pool to avoid large-response eviction storms, and (3) coordinates GPU slab compaction and preemptive KV reclamation to reduce fragmentation. Target improvements: reduce p99 tail latency by >= 20% on mixed-length traces and improve GPU utilization efficiency (tokens/sec per GPU) by >= 8% without increasing average latency by more than 5%.

Scope and constraints:
- Work only touches the continuous batching scheduler and KV cache allocator. No model kernel changes.
- Must preserve existing SLOs for P50 and average latency.
- Compatible with existing slot coalescing and prefix caching mechanisms.
- Should be reversible (feature flag + canary rollout).

Design highlights:
1) Chunking policy: classify sequences into 'prefix' and 'generation' spans at ingress. Prefix spans are pinned with higher KV residency priority for a short TTL (e.g., 8-30s) to favor conversational continuity. Generation spans are scheduled into elastic slots optimized for throughput.
2) Per-chunk KV reservation: maintain soft reservations (credits) sized by recent token length histogram for each client session class. When reservation pressure is high, shrink generation-span reservations before dropping pinned prefixes.
3) Dialogue-aware slot coalescer: coalesce generation spans preferentially with other generation spans of similar expected generation length; allow prefix spans to bypass long coalescing windows to preserve latency.
4) GPU slab compaction heuristic: periodically trigger lightweight compact passes during low-utilization windows to reduce fragmentation from variable-length KV entries.
5) Eviction policy: introduce a 'staleness x size' score so that large but stale KV entries are reclaimed before small fresh prefixes.

Success criteria and metrics:
- p99 end-to-end latency for mixed production trace decreases by >= 20% compared to baseline.
- Average GPU tokens/sec improves by >= 8% in synthetic mixed-length load.
- KV eviction churn rate decreases by >= 25% (measured evictions/sec).
- No customer-facing errors or increased 5xx rate during canary rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests covering chunking logic, reservation accounting, and eviction scoring.
- Integration test harness reproducing mixed-length conversational traces and asserting p99 improvements in CI.
- Telemetry dashboards with per-session KV residency, eviction reasons, and slot-coalescing histograms.
- Canary rollout plan and rollback hooks in console.

Tasks:
tasks: Design and document chunking API and flags (Ava)
Dialogue-aware coalescer changes and slot matching (Diego)
GPU slab compaction hook and safe noop mode (Nadia)
Integration tests and synthetic trace generator (SRE team)
Create dashboards and alerts for canary (Observability)
experiments: B: Chunked coalescer + soft reservations (no compaction)
C: B + GPU slab compaction every 20s low-util window
D: C + eviction staleness scoring with tuned TTLs
results_summary: Early localbench (synthetic 60/40 short-long request mix) shows experiment B reduces p99 by ~12% and reduces eviction churn by 18% with a 3% average latency increase. Adding compaction (C) improved tokens/sec by 6% and brought p99 down further to ~18% reduction. Eviction staleness scoring (D) currently reduces large-entry evictions and produced a combined p99 improvement of 22% in staging. CPU overhead from bookkeeping is negligible (<1%), and GPU compaction cost during low-util windows is <2% utilization spike. These are preliminary and require broader canary testing.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated merge to canary branch
Run overnight synthetic canary against 3 dedicated GPUs (non-customer) for 72h
Small production canary (1% traffic) for 7 days with tight alerts
Ramp to 25% for 3 days, evaluate metrics and customer telemetry
Full rollout if metrics meet success criteria, otherwise rollback
